target.title: docs(release): add a release-train scope contract
target.body:
Related: #73537

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's release workflow now distinguishes Code SHA and Release SHA evidence clearly, but a release train does not yet have one prospective scope record that states its goal, non-goals, allowed change classes, exit criteria, captain, and approved exceptions.

This can make an otherwise well-validated release harder to reason about when changes are considered between branch cut and publication.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a small maintainer-owned release-train contract before a new `release/YYYY.M.PATCH` branch is created, plus explicit metadata for pull requests targeting `release/**`. It complements the existing SHA-pinned validation model and keeps release inclusion decisions with maintainers.

The policy is prospective and advisory-first: normal development continues on `main`, the current release is not retroactively gated, and a required ClawSweeper check would need a completed shadow train plus separate maintainer approval.

## User Impact

Maintainers and contributors can see why a change belongs in a release train, which decision supports an exception, and what remains before the train exits. There is no runtime, package, update-channel, publication, or current-release behavior change in this PR.

## Evidence

- `pnpm docs:list`
- `pnpm check:docs`
- `git diff --check 4cbbb86d5e71aef0c953791ac0fd30caec08bf2c..a189f193613f66bdfe1d30e7c99f740b262ba6c5`
- Changed only `docs/reference/RELEASING.md` and `.agents/skills/release-openclaw-maintainer/SKILL.md`
- Tracking and rollout context: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/issues/535
